backlog.spec: Replace the fixed switch at 0.4*time_limit with an adaptive allocation. Track, for the fresh-start arm and the basin-hopping arm, the total time spent and the total improvement in best sum of radii each produced. After the first 10% of the time, choose the arm for each new run with probability proportional to (improvement + 1e-4) / (time spent + 1e-3), with a 20% floor on each arm so neither is starved. Basin hopping always perturbs the current best packing as before. Use the seeded rng for all choices.
backlog.title: Bandit time allocation between fresh starts and basin hopping

backlog.spec: In the fresh-start branch of _solve_once, give each circle a weight w_i drawn with rng: 1.0 with probability 0.75 and 0.6 with probability 0.25. Change cons_eq so circle i has radius w_i * r: pair constraints become distance - (w_i + w_j) * r, wall constraints c - w_i * r and 1 - c - w_i * r. Initial radii for the main SLSQP become w_i * max(y[-1], 0.01). Apply this to half of the fresh starts (the other half keep all weights 1). This produces mixed-size starting topologies, which the best known 32-circle packing has, without the fully random radii that failed in slot 20.
backlog.title: Two-size-class weighted common-radius stage

backlog.spec: In solve, during the late phase only, change the acceptance test from 'r.sum() > best[1].sum()' to 'r.sum() > best[1].sum() - 1e-6', while separately tracking the true best-ever packing in a second variable that is returned at the end. This lets the basin-hopping centre drift across plateaus of essentially equal packings (for example with rattlers in different positions) instead of always perturbing the same configuration. Fresh-start phase acceptance is unchanged.
backlog.title: Accept near-ties in basin hopping to drift

backlog.spec: For a fresh start, place about 4*floor(n/8) circles along the four walls first, at evenly spaced positions with small random jitter along each wall, and fill the remaining circles uniformly at random in the interior. Clip the centres to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW] and then run the usual common-radius SLSQP and main SLSQP. Half of the fresh starts use this layout and half use the existing uniform layout, selected by the rng. Boundary-heavy starts may match the wall-touching structure of the best packings.
backlog.title: Boundary-first initial placement

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, after jittering the centres, multiply the starting radii by 0.8 so the SLSQP starts strictly feasible and can re-grow circles into new arrangements instead of getting stuck on the old contact graph.
backlog.title: Basin hopping with radius-shrink before SLSQP

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, make the jitter sd depend on the circle: circles whose centre is within 0.15 of the square's boundary get sd 0.01, interior circles get sd 0.05. Interior rearrangements are expected to matter more, while boundary contacts are retained.
backlog.title: Boundary-biased perturbation

backlog.spec: In the fresh-start branch, raise the maxiter of the common-radius SLSQP from 50 to 120. The main SLSQP then starts from a better-converged equal-circle packing. This costs only 2n+1 variables per iteration, so the number of restarts should drop only a little. No other change.
backlog.title: Longer common-radius pre-solve

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres in _solve_once's fresh-start branch with a scrambled Halton sequence (bases 2 and 3) mapped into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], with a random offset and random permutation drawn from the seeded rng so each restart differs. Keep the random radius start and all other code the same. The point set is more evenly spread than uniform sampling, which may give SLSQP better starting basins.
backlog.title: Halton low-discrepancy initial centres

backlog.spec: Change MAX_ITER from 200 to 300 for all SLSQP runs, leaving everything else unchanged. Checks whether deeper convergence of each start gives better final packings at the cost of fewer restarts.
backlog.title: Replicate incumbent with MAX_ITER 300

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.5 use a different move instead of the usual jitter. Multiply all start radii by a factor drawn uniformly from [0.8,0.9], and add only a tiny centre jitter (sd 0.005). Then run the usual sparse-constraint SLSQP. The extra slack lets the contact graph rearrange without destroying the overall structure. The other half of moves keep the current sd-0.02 jitter.
backlog.title: Deflate-and-reinflate basin-hopping move

backlog.spec: Reserve the final 1 s of CPU. At that point take the best packing, run SLSQP with ftol 1e-12 and maxiter 500 from it using only pairs with gap below 0.02, then repair; keep it only if the sum of radii after repair is higher.
backlog.title: Elite LP polish in the last second

backlog.spec: Re-implement slot 14 exactly. For fresh starts, before the common-radius SLSQP, run 20 steps of 1/d^2 repulsion between centres plus repulsion from the four walls. Cap each step at 0.02 per circle and clip to [0.05,0.95]. Feed the result as the starting centres of the common-radius SLSQP. This is a replicate to check whether the -0.0030 single-run gain is real. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 14 repulsion pre-step alone

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts, after the common-radius stage assign radii by ranking: compute each circle's distance to the nearest wall or corner, and set initial radii to 0.07 for the circles nearest the centre, 0.1 for those near the middle band, and 0.08 for edge circles, plus small noise, so a large/small mix is seeded. Then run the main SLSQP.
backlog.title: Sorted-radii structured start

backlog.spec: In the common-radius stage used for fresh starts, add a small quadratic term -0.05 * sum((r_i - mean(r))^2) to the objective so the optimiser prefers slightly more uniform radii before the main SLSQP. Remove the term for the main stage so the final objective is exactly the sum of radii. The regulariser is only a smoothing device to escape the flat direction in the radius block and must not change the final objective. Keep the code change to a few lines.
backlog.title: Dual-scale radius regulariser inside the first SLSQP stage

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.02 and INIT_LOW to 0.05 in the fresh-start common-radius stage so that SLSQP starts from a feasible, non-overlapping-ish configuration and the early iterations are less constrained.
backlog.title: Smaller initial common radius

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.3, perturb the best packing differently. Rotate all centres about (0.5,0.5) by an angle drawn uniformly from plus or minus [2,6] degrees, then add Gaussian jitter of sd 0.005, clip to [0.01,0.99], and multiply the radii by 0.95. Then run the usual sparse SLSQP. Otherwise use the existing jitter move. The rotation shifts all wall contacts together, which local jitter rarely does.
backlog.title: Small rotation move about the square centre

backlog.spec: Change INIT_LOW from 0.1 to 0.03. Fresh random centres are then drawn from [0.03,0.97] instead of [0.1,0.9]. Good packings put many circles against the walls and in the corners, and starting them there may cut the distance the common-radius stage must move them. No other change.
backlog.title: Lower INIT_LOW so random starts reach walls and corners

backlog.spec: Combine the two best single-run variants (slots 14 and 25), which have not been tried together. (a) In _solve_once for fresh starts, before the common-radius SLSQP, apply 20 steps of pairwise 1/d^2 repulsion to the random centres: for each step compute the force sum over j of (c_i - c_j)/|c_i - c_j|^3, scale so the largest displacement is 0.02, add it, and clip to [0.02, 0.98]. (b) In solve, during the late phase keep a 'current' packing separate from 'best': perturb current (not best), accept the new packing as current if its sum is higher or with probability exp((new - cur)/0.002) using rng, and always update best when improved. Return best.
backlog.title: Combine repulsion pre-step with Metropolis chain

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, build the initial centres from a 6x6 grid of cell centres ((k+0.5)/6). Choose 32 of the 36 cells at random with rng, and add uniform jitter of plus or minus 0.3 cell widths. Then run 20 steps of 1/d^2 pairwise and wall repulsion, with per-circle displacement capped at 0.02 and centres clipped to [0.05,0.95]. Use the result as y0 for the existing common-radius SLSQP. The basin-hopping phase is unchanged.
backlog.title: Combine repulsion pre-step (slot 14) with jittered 6x6 grid starts (slot 10)

backlog.spec: In the start-is-not-None branch of _solve_once, scale the Gaussian jitter per circle inversely to its radius: sd_i = 0.02 * (mean(r0) / max(r0_i, 0.02)) clipped to [0.01, 0.06], and use c0 = clip(start[0] + rng.normal(size=(n, 2)) * sd_i[:, None], 0.01, 0.99). Small circles, which sit in holes and are cheap to move, get large moves; the large load-bearing circles are barely disturbed. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Radius-dependent jitter size

memo:
Helped: search-strategy changes only. Slot 4 (basin-hopping from jittered copies of the best packing after 40% of the time) gave -0.0050 over 2 runs. Slot 7 (cheap common-radius SLSQP init for fresh starts) gave -0.0063 over 2 runs. The incumbent is -2.9366, about 0.0004 below the published 2.9370, so little headroom remains.

Did not help: constraint reformulation (slot 0, +0.0140), analytic Jacobians (+0.0007), final polish (+0.0049), mirror starts (+0.0014), L-BFGS-B penalty init (+0.0056), per-circle random radii (+0.0081). Nearly all later single-run tweaks sit within noise (sd about 0.0034). The best were slots 14 and 25 (-0.0030 each) and slot 10 (-0.0020). Several were aborted as duplicates.

Next: replicate the incumbent first. Then replicate slots 14, 25 and 10 and try combining them. Avoid repeating tried ideas. Keep the code simple. Further gains are likely below the noise level, so consider stopping.
